items.prompt: Given a list of distinct tags, return every possible set of tags (including the empty set).
items.why: Every combination is an answer and nothing is ever ruled out → BFS subsets from the empty set. Backtracking is for when constraints kill branches early; here there's nothing to prune.

items.prompt: Given an array that may contain repeated numbers, return all subsets without listing the same subset twice.
items.why: All subsets + duplicates in the input → sort, then extend only the subsets created in the previous step. Knapsack would only count or optimise, not list them.

items.prompt: Given a string of letters and digits, return every string you get by switching any of the letters between lowercase and uppercase.
items.why: Each letter is an independent two-way choice and every combination is valid → subsets: each letter doubles the list of strings.

items.prompt: Can an array of positive integers (n ≤ 200, values ≤ 100) be split into two groups with equal sums?
items.why: Only a yes/no about some subset, and n is too big for 2ⁿ → 0/1 knapsack DP over (item, sum). Listing subsets would be exponential.

items.prompt: Return every combination of the given distinct numbers (each usable many times) that adds up to a target.
items.why: List combinations that must satisfy a constraint (the sum) → backtracking: abandon a partial combination as soon as it overshoots. Unbounded knapsack would only count them.

items.prompt: Count the contiguous subarrays of positive integers whose product is less than k.
items.why: Contiguous + a running constraint (product < k) → dynamic sliding window. A subarray isn't an arbitrary subset.

items.prompt: Return every subsequence of a short string (length ≤ 12), duplicates allowed.
items.why: List all subsequences = all subsets of positions → subsets. The DP patterns are for the longest/count of subsequences, and sliding window needs contiguity.
